newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks lower ahead of Jospin speech.
newsitem.headline: French stocks lower ahead of Jospin speech.

text.p: French stocks were lower in quiet early trading on Thursday ahead of new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote policy speech to parliament scheduled to begin at 1300 GMT.
"The market's waiting for Jospin but also watching to see how Wall Street performs. The market's short on ideas for the moment," a trader said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which has risen sharply since the election at the start of the month of a Socialist-led government, was down 12.06 points, or 0.44 percent, at 2,739.68 at 0900 GMT. The CAC-40 June futures contract was down 11 points at 2,737.
Volume was a modest 540 million francs.
Shares in luxury goods group LVMH extended their loss, slipping 0.4 percent, after the French company stepped up its fight against proposed merger partners Guinness and Grand Met.
Appliance firm Moulinex's stock was up 3.4 percent at 147.90 francs after the company reported its first annual profit since 1991 on Wednesday evening.
